newsitem.title: USA: "Hollywood Madam" Fleiss sentenced to 37 months.
newsitem.headline: "Hollywood Madam" Fleiss sentenced to 37 months.

text.p: Reputed "Hollywood Madam" Heidi Fleiss, who ran a call-girl ring catering to the movie industry's rich and famous, was sentenced on Tuesday to 37 months in federal prison for tax evasion and money laundering.
Judge Consuelo Marshall could have sentenced her to more than eight years under federal guidelines for the eight counts on which she had been convicted.
But the judge said she was more lenient because she agreed with defence lawyers that the legal system was sexually biased by only punishing women in prostitution cases.

Marshall also ordered Fleiss to perform 300 hours of community service and pay $400 in court costs but said she would recommend Fleiss be credited with the four to five months she has already spent in prison and in drug rehabilitation.
Wishing Fleiss good luck, Marshall said: "I think you are strong enough to serve this sentence."

"(After release) You will be a positive role model for the young people and other women," said the judge, who also ordered Fleiss to undergo three years of supervised probation once she is relased from prison.
Fleiss' lawyers, who had argued she was a victim of abusive relationships and suffered from attention deficit disorder, said they were satisfied with the sentence and did not plan to appeal.
"It's OK, it's OK. I'm OK," Fleiss, appearing emotionally-drained, told her weeping brothers and sisters as she was led out of the packed courtroom.
"Be strong," shouted her teenage brother, Jesse, while her father, Paul Fleiss, whispered "Jesus!" under his breath.
In a tearful appeal to the judge before sentencing, Fleiss had begged for leniency. Choking on her words, she said:"I am a different person now. I made terrible choices and mistakes."
Fleiss had been convicted in August 1995, but her sentencing was delayed after she was arrested last year for violating bail by smoking methamphetamines.

In addition to the federal conviction, Fleiss was also convicted in state court of pandering, but that conviction was overturned by an appeals court on the basis of jury misconduct, and the judge has ordered a retrial.
Fleiss' attorney, Daniel Marks, told reporters afterwards that he would use the federal sentencing in his argument for the state case to be dropped when it is scheduled to start on Monday.
Judge Marshall explained that in imposing a lenient sentence, she took into consideration the defence argument that the justice system was sexually biased in cases involving prostitution.
In addition to the sentence passed on Tuesday, the government has already seized some of Fleiss' assets, including a house valued at $375,000 and more than $177,000 in cash from her accounts.
